necessary.title: Necessary
necessary.description: States a needed capability or constraint; removing it leaves the product incomplete. If nothing breaks without it, it is superfluous.

implementation_free.title: Implementation-free
implementation_free.description: Says what, not how: does not impose architecture, technology, storage format or protocol without a real need.

unambiguous.title: Unambiguous
unambiguous.description: Can be read only one way: no vague words, undefined terms, unspecified units, time zones or interval bounds.

complete.title: Complete
complete.description: Needs no guessing: conditions, error handling and edge cases are described; no “to be defined later”.

singular.title: Singular
singular.description: One requirement — one capability or constraint; no “and/or” bundling several behaviours.

feasible.title: Feasible
feasible.description: Achievable within reasonable technical, time and budget constraints.

verifiable.title: Verifiable
verifiable.description: A finite objective way (test, analysis, inspection) exists to prove it; measurable criteria are given.

correct.title: Correct
correct.description: Accurately reflects the stakeholder need and the domain; contains no factual errors.

conforming.title: Conforming
conforming.description: Follows the agreed template and style of the document.

traceable.title: Traceable
traceable.description: Has an identifier and a clear source; tests and child documents can refer to it.

set_complete.title: Complete (set)
set_complete.description: The set covers all needed capabilities, errors, states and interfaces; template sections are filled in.

set_consistent.title: Consistent
set_consistent.description: Requirements do not contradict each other, acceptance criteria or child documents; terms and units are used uniformly.

set_feasible.title: Feasible (set)
set_feasible.description: The set as a whole is achievable within project constraints.

set_comprehensible.title: Comprehensible
set_comprehensible.description: It is clear what the system is expected to do and how it relates to its environment.

set_validatable.title: Able to be validated
set_validatable.description: It can be shown that meeting the set satisfies the business need.

set_ranked.title: Ranked
set_ranked.description: Importance and/or stability is stated for requirements.

set_modifiable.title: Modifiable
set_modifiable.description: The structure allows changes without duplication; the document is versioned.

set_traceable.title: Traceable (set)
set_traceable.description: Links between requirements, acceptance criteria and child documents can be followed.

auth.title: The provider rejected the API key
auth.hint: Check the key in Settings: it may be truncated, revoked or issued for another project.

forbidden.title: No access to the model
forbidden.hint: The key works, but the account has no access to this model or region. Pick another model or enable access in the provider console.

rate_limit.title: Too many requests (provider limit)
rate_limit.hint: Free tiers limit requests per minute. Increase the pause between calls (5–10 s), set concurrency to 1 and run again.

quota.title: Quota exhausted or billing missing
quota.hint: The daily limit or account balance has run out. Top up, wait for the quota reset or switch provider.

not_found.title: Model not found at the provider
not_found.hint: Pick a model from the list in Settings. If the list is empty, check the key or server address.

bad_request.title: The provider rejected the request
bad_request.hint: Usually a parameter the selected model does not support. Try another model; if it persists, pass the details to an administrator.

context.title: The document does not fit the model context
context.hint: Reduce the batch size in AI parameters or pick a model with a larger context.

timeout.title: The model did not answer in time
timeout.hint: Local and reasoning models are slow. Increase the run timeout in AI parameters or reduce the batch size.

connection.title: Cannot reach the provider
connection.hint: The model server is unreachable from ReqCheck. Check the base URL, the server and the proxy.

unavailable.title: The provider is temporarily unavailable
unavailable.hint: The provider is overloaded or failing. Wait a couple of minutes and run again; you can also raise the number of attempts.

invalid_output.title: The model returned malformed output
invalid_output.hint: Weaker models sometimes break JSON. Reduce the batch size, raise the attempts or pick a stronger model.

not_configured.title: The provider is not configured
not_configured.hint: Set a key (for a local model — the server address) in Settings.

not_implemented.title: This agent feature is not ready yet
not_implemented.hint: This part of the core is not implemented on the server yet. Tell an administrator.

cancelled.title: Run cancelled
cancelled.hint: The run was stopped by a user or by timeout. You can run it again.

unknown.title: Error while calling the model
unknown.hint: See the details below. If it persists, pass them to an administrator.

modelNotFound.title: Model “{{model}}” not found at the provider
modelNotFound.hint: The key works, but the provider has no such model (or the account cannot use it). Pick a model from the “Default model” list and save.

params.defaultsHint: Used for new runs and chat when nothing else is chosen.
params.pacingHint: Tune to the provider plan: free keys are rate-limited, local models are slow.

preset.free_geminiHint: 6 s pause, 1 worker, 8 attempts — to stay clear of 429
preset.paid_apiHint: No pause, 4 workers, batches of 8 — fast
preset.localHint: 1 worker, batches of 3, 4 attempts, 1 h run timeout — for a single GPU

min_interval_s.label: Pause between calls
min_interval_s.hint: Free Gemini and 429 “Too many requests” errors — set 5–10 s. Paid plans and local models — 0.

concurrency.label: Parallel requests
concurrency.hint: Paid APIs — 3–4, runs get several times faster. Free keys and a local model on one GPU — 1, otherwise 429 or queueing.

max_attempts.label: Attempts per call
max_attempts.hint: Retries on 429, 5xx and network drops. 4–6 is usually enough; 8 on free tiers. More means longer hangs on real failures.

batch_size.label: Requirements per request
batch_size.hint: Bigger — fewer and cheaper calls, but weak models break JSON more often. On format or context errors drop to 3–4.

run_timeout_s.label: Whole run timeout
run_timeout_s.hint: Runs longer than this stop with an error. Local and reasoning models, large documents — 3600 s or more (up to 6 h).

params.embeddingsHint: The model that turns text into vectors for semantic search over runs and the knowledge base.

emb.localHint: Works offline, data never leaves. Recommended for a bank perimeter.
emb.geminiHint: Better on long texts, but texts are sent to Google.
emb.openaiHint: Paid, texts are sent to OpenAI.

params.reindexWarning: After changing the embeddings model the knowledge base and run history are re-indexed — search may be incomplete for a few minutes.

max_upload_mb.label: Upload size limit
max_upload_mb.hint: Maximum size of a document or knowledge-base file. Scanned PDFs can be heavy — 50–100 MB.

session_ttl_hours.label: Session lifetime
session_ttl_hours.hint: Hours until the user has to sign in again. For a shared computer — 1–2 h.

params.embDimHint: Gemini only. 768 balances quality and index size.
params.embModelBuiltin: Default: the embeddings service built-in model

parsing.role: Reads PDF, DOCX, MD and TXT, normalises the text and keeps offsets that quotes are later checked against.

segmenting.role: Extracts requirements and acceptance criteria: an LLM plus hints from IDs, acceptance lines and API response codes. Splits compound ones into sub-requirements.

rule_checks.role: Rules without an LLM: vague words in Russian and English, TBD markers, empty template fields, document version.

checking_requirements.role: Checks every requirement against the 10 criteria of ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 5.2.5 and IEEE 830 4.3, in batches, with knowledge base snippets.

checking_set.role: Six reviewers with different roles look at the whole set: two consistency controllers (rule logic and spec consistency), a systems analyst, a QA analyst, an integration architect, and a risk and security analyst.

verifying.role: Checks quotes against the text by code, then the verifier tries to refute every finding, aligns severity and merges duplicates in two passes.

rendering.role: Prepares clarifying questions for the author and writes the conclusion: can development and testing start, what to fix first. Builds MD, DOCX, PDF and JSON exports.

questions.emptyHint: The agent found nothing that needs the author's decision, or questions were turned off.
questions.intro: Without answers to these questions the team cannot implement and test the requirements unambiguously. Blockers first.

agentsPage.title: Agents
agentsPage.subtitle: How ReqCheck checks a document: run stages, LLM agents and code checks. Click an agent to see its role, inputs, outputs and links.

details.title: About the agent
details.pick: Pick an agent in the pipeline
details.pickHint: You will see what it does, what it receives and who gets its result. Related agents are highlighted.

agentsPage.reviewerNote: Six reviewers work in parallel and look at the whole requirement set. Each first writes working notes (up to 350 words), then states defects for its criteria and may suggest a question for the author.
agentsPage.reviewerInput: Requirement list, the whole document, set defects already found by rules
agentsPage.reviewerOutput: Set defects, verdicts for its criteria, questions for the author

document.name: Document
document.role: The requirements file the user uploaded. It is stored in S3; a Celery worker performs the run.
document.how:
POST /api/documents puts the file into S3, POST /api/runs queues the task.
The worker downloads the file and takes model settings from the account page; keys are stored encrypted in Postgres.
Run options go to the core: batch size, concurrency, verifier, questions for the author.

knowledge.name: Knowledge base
knowledge.role: The bank's glossary, templates and rules. Before a run the worker finds fragments close to the document and passes them to the agents.
knowledge.output: Up to 6 fragments in the system prompt
knowledge.how:
Notes are split into fragments and indexed in Qdrant.
The worker searches by the first 3,000 characters of the document; the core already knows the built-in standards summary.
Fragments go into the system prompt of every LLM agent in the run and of the report chat.

parser.name: Parsing
parser.role: Reads PDF, DOCX, MD and TXT and normalizes the text. All report locations and quotes are offsets in this text.
parser.output: Normalized text with page bounds and headings
parser.how:
For PDF, page bounds are kept so each defect has a page number.
Section headings are found by code; they are used for splitting and for location labels in the report.
A PDF without a text layer gives a clear error: there is no OCR yet.

segmenter.name: Splitter
segmenter.role: Picks out individual requirements and numbers them R-001… Compound requirements are split into parts R-002.1, R-002.2.
segmenter.input: Document text and candidates found by code
segmenter.output: Requirement list with locations in the text
segmenter.how:
A long document is cut by headings into fragments of up to 40,000 characters, one request each.
Code finds candidates beforehand (numbered items, “F-N”, table rows) and hints them to the model.
Code looks up each model requirement in the text; missing ones are dropped, 80% overlaps are merged.
Candidates the model missed are added from the code hints.

rules.name: Rules
rules.role: Deterministic checks: vague words, “TBD” and “to be filled in later”, empty template fields and rows, unfilled checklist, missing document version, compound requirements.
rules.how:
Works the same on every run and spends no tokens.
Findings go to the inspector and reviewers as “already found” so the model does not repeat them.
The verifier cannot reject a rule defect, only change its severity.

inspector.name: Requirement inspector
inspector.role: Checks each requirement against the 10 criteria of ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 5.2.5 and IEEE 830 4.3: necessary, unambiguous, complete, verifiable and others.
inspector.input: A batch of requirements, the whole document, rule findings for these requirements
inspector.output: Requirement defects and criteria not applicable to a requirement
inspector.how:
Requirements go in batches (6 by default); batches run in parallel per the concurrency setting.
The request includes the whole document so the model sees the context.
The model may mark a criterion as not applicable, then it does not count as failed.
Progress is reported per requirement: the run screen shows “12 of 42”.

logic.name: Business logic controller
logic.role: Looks for conflicts between business rules and between rules and acceptance criteria.
logic.how:
Lists the rules as “condition → result” and compares pairs that touch the same object.
Recomputes every acceptance criterion using the document's rules: dates, amounts, limits.
Checks the document goal and process diagrams against the rules.

contract.name: Specification consistency controller
contract.role: Looks for mismatches between the main document and API and data specifications, inside contracts, in terms and units.
contract.how:
Checks method, URL, parameters, response codes and examples in the API specification.
Checks that one value has one type and format in request, response and storage.
Looks for one rule described differently in different places.

analyst.name: Systems analyst
analyst.role: Looks for what is missing: alternative scenarios, errors, entity life cycle, glossary, priorities, version and change history.
analyst.how:
Walks each function through main and alternative scenarios, errors, limits and cancellation.
Looks for combinations of rules that are not described anywhere.
Checks message texts, UI states and input validation.

qa.name: Test analyst
qa.role: Judges whether tests can be designed from the document: do requirements have acceptance criteria and is the result observable.
qa.how:
Finds functional requirements without acceptance criteria.
Checks that preconditions are complete and the expected result is unambiguous.
Names missing negative and boundary checks and measurable thresholds.

architect.name: Integration architect
architect.role: Checks traceability “goal → requirements → interfaces → data → acceptance” and feasibility at the system level.
architect.how:
Matches operations in the main document and child specifications.
Reviews HTTP methods, idempotency, error format, data model.
Looks for undescribed races, redelivery, unavailable neighbour systems, rollback.

security.name: Risk and security analyst
security.role: Reads the document as the bank's information security: personal and payment data, authorization, audit, operational risks.
security.how:
Checks what ends up in notifications, URLs and logs, and whether it is masked.
Looks for resource ownership checks and brute-force protection.
Assesses risks of false or unsent notifications and of release rollback.

quotes.name: Quote check
quotes.short: every quote is in the text
quotes.role: Code looks up every quote the model gave in the document text. A found quote gets an exact location, page number and a “verified” mark.
quotes.input: Defect candidates from rules, the inspector and reviewers
quotes.output: Defects with verified locations, without exact duplicates
quotes.how:
First a search normalizing spaces, quotes and case, then a fuzzy one.
If a quote is not found, the defect is tied to the requirement's location with a note; without a requirement it is dropped.
Then code merges defects with the same location and criterion.

verifier.name: Verifier
verifier.role: An independent re-check agent: tries to refute each defect against the document text and aligns severity.
verifier.input: All defect candidates and the document
verifier.output: Keep / drop decision and severity for each
verifier.how:
Defects go in groups of 20, groups run in parallel; unanswered ones are retried in groups of 8.
Drops misreadings, generic phrases and formal nitpicks; keeps gaps and conflicts.
Does not drop rule defects, only changes severity. Without a model answer the defect stays.
Enabled by the “Verifier” option (on by default).

merger.name: Duplicate merger
merger.role: Different agents find the same problem independently. This agent groups findings where fixing one closes the others.
merger.output: Duplicate groups, one entry per group
merger.how:
Two passes: over the whole list and separately over findings about one place in the document.
Code merges a group only if findings are related: same place, shared requirement or same set criterion.
When in doubt the model does not merge.

checklist.name: Checklist
checklist.role: If the document has a requirements review checklist, answers each item based on the check, with links to defects.
checklist.how:
Enabled by the “Fill in the review checklist” option.
Without a model answer, code fills the item from the defects found.

questions.name: Questions for the author
questions.role: Prepares clarifying questions the team cannot start or test without: closed, with 2–4 answer options, an addressee and a priority.
questions.input: Defects and questions suggested by reviewers
questions.how:
Questions about the same thing are merged; each lists related defects D-xxx.
Priority: blocker, important, minor; addressee: product owner, analyst, architect, security and others.
Without a model answer, reviewers' questions are used.

conclusion.name: Conclusion
conclusion.role: Writes the conclusion: is the document ready for development and for testing, why, and what to fix first.
conclusion.how:
Takes into account critical defects and failures of individual check batches.
A failed batch does not stop the run but is noted in the rationale.

report.name: Report
report.role: Code assembles the report: run passport, requirements, verdicts for 18 criteria, defects D-001…, checklist, questions, summary and conclusion.
report.how:
Defects are sorted by requirement order, then by severity, and numbered D-001…
MD, DOCX and PDF exports are stored in S3, the report in Postgres.
Requirements and defects are indexed in Qdrant — Search finds them.

chat.name: Report chat
chat.role: Answers questions about a finished report as a text stream. Sees the report, the document text and knowledge base fragments.
chat.input: Report, document, conversation history, knowledge base
chat.how:
The API calls it directly, without the worker, and streams the answer (SSE).
The context includes requirements, all defects with quotes and up to 60,000 characters of the document.
Remembers the last 20 messages of the conversation.

known.title: Shared list of findings
known.text: Each next agent receives what is already found, marked “do not repeat”: rules → inspector → reviewers.

schema.title: Structured answers only
schema.text: The model answers with JSON in a strict schema: the provider's native mode, a tool call or a schema in the prompt. Temperature 0, retry on errors.

quotes.title: Code checks quotes
quotes.text: The model must quote verbatim. Code finds the quote in the text; a defect not backed by the text does not reach the report.

refute.title: Independent re-check
refute.text: One agent finds, another checks. The verifier looks for why a defect is wrong, not why it is right.

parallel.title: Parallel where possible
parallel.text: Inspector batches, the six reviewers and verifier groups run in parallel, per the concurrency setting on the account page.

failures.title: A partial failure does not stop the run
failures.text: A batch without an answer is noted in the conclusion. The run stops at once only on a settings error: no key, 401, 403, 404.

progress.title: Live progress
progress.text: Agents report each step; the worker publishes events to Redis and the API passes them to the run screen.

kb.title: Bank knowledge in every request
kb.text: Knowledge base fragments go into the system prompt of all LLM agents and of the report chat.

agentsPage.matrixTitle: Who is responsible for which criteria
agentsPage.matrixHint: Columns are the agents that look for defects. The verifier re-checks defects for all criteria.
agentsPage.flowHint: From finding to a number in the report.

found.title: Finding
found.text: Rules, the inspector or a reviewer find a defect: quote, criterion, severity, suggestion.

quote.title: Quote found
quote.text: Code finds the quote in the text and sets the exact location; otherwise the requirement's location with a note.

dedupe.title: Exact duplicates
dedupe.text: Code merges defects with the same location and criterion.

verify.title: Re-check
verify.text: The verifier keeps or drops the defect and aligns severity.

merge.title: Merge
merge.text: One problem from different agents becomes one entry.

number.title: Number D-xxx
number.text: Sorting by requirements and severity, numbering, criteria verdicts.

use.title: In the report
use.text: The defect feeds the checklist, questions for the author, the conclusion and the chat.
